issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement uses the class name 'Course' while the rest of the exercise (text, template, and solution) refer to the class as 'Lecture'. This naming mismatch in the problem statement's UML can confuse students about which class they should implement and where the listed attributes/methods belong.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the UML diagram from 'Course' to 'Lecture' in problem_statement.md so it matches the exercise text, the template, and the solution. Ensure the UML header and any references inside the diagram consistently use 'Lecture' to avoid confusing students.

This mismatched class name (Course vs Lecture) is a naming inconsistency that can confuse students when mapping the UML to the provided Lecture.java template and the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the UML class name with the rest of the exercise by renaming the UML class from 'Course' to 'Lecture' in problem_statement.md (so students can directly map the UML attributes to Lecture.java). Alternatively, change textual references to use 'Course' consistently, but preferably update the UML to 'Lecture'.
